collection.descriptionHtml:
Grundfos circulator pumps and pump connection parts. The collection includes UPS15-58FC and UPSe ECM cast iron circulators for closed heating loops, UPS15-55SFC and UPS26-99SFC stainless steel models, ALPHA and ALPHA2 variable speed ECM circulators, MAGNA1 and MAGNA3 circulators with listed heads up to 59 ft and flows up to 85 gpm, UP15-18 bronze circulators with 1/2" and 3/4" sweat connections, the UP15-10SU7P Comfort and ALPHA HWR hot water recirculation pumps and the Comfort valve. Connection parts include cast iron and bronze pump flange sets from 3/4" to 1-1/2", union sets, clip-on aquastat kits and timer kits.

Use cast iron bodies on closed hydronic loops, and bronze or stainless steel for potable water and recirculation.

How to choose

  • Flow and head: size the pump by the required flow and head. Titles list maximum figures on several models, such as 19 ft and 18 gpm on the UPS15-58FC and 33 ft and 42 gpm on the UPSe 26-99F.
  • Body material: cast iron for closed heating loops; bronze or stainless steel for potable water.
  • Connection: pumps are listed as flanged, union or sweat. Match the flange or union set to the pump model and the pipe size.
  • Voltage: most models are listed at 115 V; MAGNA models are listed at 115 V or 115-230 V.
  • Recirculation control: recirculation pumps are listed with a timer and line cord, and clip-on aquastat kits are sold separately for UP series pumps.

Common questions

Cast iron or stainless steel Grundfos circulator?

Use cast iron on closed hydronic heating loops. Use bronze or stainless steel for potable water and hot water recirculation, such as the UPS26-99SFC.

How do I pick the right flanges for a Grundfos pump?

Match the flange or union set to the pump model and the pipe size. See pump flanges.

How do I size a circulator?

Size the pump from the flow and head loss of the loop, not from pressure. An oversized pump is noisy and an undersized one leaves cold zones. See all circulator pumps.

Related collections: circulator pumps, variable speed circulators, hot water recirculating pumps, pump flanges and accessories and hydronic centrifugal pumps.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Copper press fittings join copper tube with a press tool instead of solder: the jaw compresses the fitting onto the tube and an EPDM sealing element makes the seal. No flame and no flux are needed. This collection holds Viega ProPress fittings and Mueller Streamline copper press fittings in 1/2" through 4", in press x press, press x FTG, press x FIP, press x MIP and press x flange.

Fitting bodies are copper, with brass or bronze where the fitting transitions to a thread or flange. Reducing tees are the largest group, followed by fitting reducers, reducing couplings, unions, male and female adapters, couplings, 45° and 90° elbows, street elbows and caps. Both lines are made for ASTM B88 Type K, L and M copper tube.

How to choose

  • Tube type and size. Viega ProPress and Mueller Streamline press fittings are for Type K, L and M hard copper tube in 1/2" to 4", and soft copper in 1/2" to 1-1/4". Our copper pipe and tube specifications cover wall thickness by type.
  • Connection ends. P is a press end that accepts tube. FTG is a fitting end, sized like tube, that slides into another press socket. FPT/FIP and MPT/MIP are threaded ends for valves and equipment.
  • Sealing element. The fittings here ship with EPDM sealing elements. Check the manufacturer's application list for the fluid and temperature before using them on anything other than water.
  • Standard and tool. Press-connect copper fittings are covered by ASME B16.51. Use the press tool and jaws the fitting manufacturer approves for that line and size. Our press fitting technical specifications list seal compounds, standards and jaw compatibility.

Common questions

What copper tube can be used with ProPress fittings?

Viega lists ProPress for Type K, L and M hard copper tube from 1/2" to 4" and soft copper tube from 1/2" to 1-1/4". The tube is cut square, deburred and marked for insertion depth before pressing.

What does Viega Smart Connect do?

Smart Connect is a feature on Viega ProPress fittings that lets an unpressed fitting be identified during pressure testing. Viega states it does not replace the pressure test required by code.

What is the difference between a P end and an FTG end?

A P (press) end is a socket with a sealing element that accepts tube. An FTG end has the outside diameter of tube and goes into the press socket of another fitting, which is how street elbows and fitting reducers connect without a short piece of tube.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Viega MegaPress is a press-connection system for IPS steel pipe. Instead of threading, grooving or welding, the installer slides the fitting onto the pipe and closes it with a press tool, which keeps open flame off the job.

This collection gathers every MegaPress item we list in 1/2" through 4": couplings, elbows, tees, reducers, threaded adapters, caps, unions, flanges, transition couplings and ball valves. It includes standard MegaPress fittings in zinc-nickel coated carbon steel, MegaPressG fittings with an HNBR sealing element for fuel gas, and MegaPress 316 fittings for stainless steel pipe. The connection is spelled out in each title, for example P-P for press by press, P-MPT for press by male thread and FTG(IPS) for a street end.

How to choose

  • Fitting family. Standard MegaPress for water and hydronic piping, MegaPressG for fuel gas and fuel oil, MegaPress 316 where stainless steel pipe is specified. The family name is in every product title.
  • Pipe. Viega lists MegaPress for Schedule 5 to Schedule 40 carbon steel pipe to ASTM A53, A106, A135 and A795. Confirm the schedule Viega allows for your application, since fuel gas has its own requirement.
  • Sealing element. MegaPressG uses HNBR; standard MegaPress uses EPDM. They are not interchangeable between gas and water service.
  • Ends and size. P x P, P x FPT, P x MPT, P x flange or FTG(IPS) x P, in 1/2" to 4". Reducing tees and street reducers list every size in the title.
  • Tool. MegaPress is installed with compatible press tools and MegaPress jaws or rings. Check your tool before ordering.

Common questions

What is the difference between MegaPress and MegaPressG?

The sealing element. MegaPressG fittings have a factory-installed HNBR sealing element for fuel gas and fuel oil; standard MegaPress fittings have an EPDM sealing element for water and hydronic service. Use the family rated for the fluid.

What pipe does MegaPress work with?

Viega lists MegaPress for Schedule 5 to Schedule 40 carbon steel pipe conforming to ASTM A53, A106, A135 and A795. MegaPress 316 is the version for stainless steel pipe.

How does a MegaPress fitting hold the pipe?

Each press end contains a sealing element, a 304 stainless steel separator ring and a 420 stainless steel grip ring. Pressing closes the grip ring onto the pipe and compresses the sealing element.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Gas press fittings join steel pipe for fuel gas without threading: the fitting is pressed onto the pipe with a jaw tool and sealed with a sealing element made for fuel gas. No cutting oil, no die head and no rotating the pipe.

This collection holds Viega MegaPressG and Mueller Streamline carbon steel gas press fittings in 1/2" through 4", in press, press x FTG, press x FIP, press x MIP and press x flange. Reducing tees, fitting reducers, couplings, 90° and 45° elbows, street elbows, male and female adapters, caps and unions make up the range.

The sealing element is what makes these gas fittings. Viega MegaPressG uses HNBR, while water press fittings use EPDM, and the two are not substitutes. Confirm the fitting is marked for gas before installing it.

How to choose

  • Pipe. Check the pipe material and schedule the fitting manufacturer allows for fuel gas before ordering.
  • Sealing element. Viega MegaPressG uses HNBR for fuel gas and fuel oil. Do not use an EPDM water fitting on gas.
  • Listing. Use fittings the manufacturer lists for fuel gas. Your local code and gas utility decide where press fittings are accepted.
  • Ends and size. P x P for pipe-to-pipe joints, FTG x P for street elbows and reducers, FPT and MPT for appliances and valves, flange for flanged connections.
  • Tool and brand. Match the fitting brand to press jaws approved for it. Our press fitting technical specifications cover seal selection, listings and pipe schedules.

Common questions

Can press fittings be used on natural gas?

Yes, when the fitting is listed for fuel gas, as Viega MegaPressG is. Acceptance still depends on the local fuel gas code and the gas utility.

How do I tell a gas press fitting from a water press fitting?

By the product line and marking. Viega gas fittings are named MegaPressG and carry an HNBR sealing element; Mueller Streamline gas part numbers in this collection end in G. Water and hydronic versions use EPDM.

What sizes do gas press fittings come in?

This collection covers 1/2", 3/4", 1", 1-1/4", 1-1/2", 2", 2-1/2", 3" and 4", including reducing tees and street reducers between those sizes.

Related: Viega MegaPress fittings, black iron threaded fittings, flexible gas fittings, gas valves, press tools and jaws.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Viega PureFlow press fittings connect PEX tubing with a stainless steel sleeve that is closed by a press tool. This collection covers PureFlow Press in Zero Lead bronze and polymer (shown as Brass and Composite in many product titles), in 3/8" through 2", with press, press x copper, press x FTG, press x FIP and press x flare ends.

Each fitting has Viega Smart Connect: a fitting that was not pressed is identified during the pressure test, so it can be found before the wall is closed. The range runs reducing tees, 90° elbows, couplings, reducing couplings, male and female adapters, drop ear elbows, plugs and manifold tees, with reducing tees the deepest group. Adapters to ProPress and to copper sweat cover transitions to copper tube.

How to choose

  • Tubing size. 1/2", 3/4" and 1" are the common sizes; the line continues to 1-1/4", 1-1/2" and 2". Reducing tees list run x run x branch in the title.
  • Body material. Zero Lead bronze or polymer. Viega's polymer fittings are polyphenylsulfone; both carry a 304 stainless steel press sleeve.
  • Connection ends. Press x press for PEX to PEX; press x ProPress, press x copper sweat (C or FTG), press x FIP/MIP and press x flare for transitions.
  • Standard. Viega certifies its sleeved PureFlow Press fittings to ASTM F877. Use them with PEX tubing the manufacturer lists for the system.
  • Tool. PureFlow Press needs a PureFlow press tool or jaws; a transition fitting to ProPress needs both the PureFlow and the ProPress jaws.

Common questions

What is the difference between PureFlow press and crimp fittings?

PureFlow Press fittings come with a stainless steel sleeve attached and are closed with a press tool. PureFlow Crimp fittings are insert fittings secured with a separate copper crimp ring and a crimp tool. They are separate lines with separate tools.

Are Viega PureFlow fittings lead free?

Viega describes its Zero Lead bronze fittings as meeting NSF/ANSI 372, at 0.25% or less weighted average lead content. Viega notes that its 5/16" and 5/8" bronze fittings are not Zero Lead and are for radiant systems only.

What does Smart Connect do on a PureFlow fitting?

It lets an unpressed connection be identified during pressure testing. It does not replace the pressure test.

Related: Viega PureFlow crimp fittings, all PEX fittings, PEX manifolds, PEX tools and the full Viega range.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Viega PureFlow crimp fittings are insert fittings for PEX tubing, secured with a copper crimp ring and a crimp tool. This collection covers the PureFlow Crimp line in 3/8" through 1", in composite (polymer) and brass.

It includes tees and reducing tees, couplings and reducing couplings, 90° elbows, drop ear elbows and plugs, plus male and female threaded adapters, copper sweat adapters, and PEX to polybutylene transition couplings. Product titles identify the connection, for example Crimp x MIP or Crimp x FIP, and the body material.

Crimp fittings are joined with copper crimp rings and a calibrated crimp tool, so confirm the tool matches the ring size and check each joint with a go/no-go gauge.

How to choose

  • Tubing size. 3/8", 1/2", 3/4" and 1". Reducing tees and couplings list each end in the title.
  • Body material. Composite for most tees, elbows, couplings and plugs; brass for threaded and sweat adapters, drop ear elbows and some tees.
  • Other end. Crimp x crimp for PEX to PEX; crimp x MIP or FIP for threaded connections; crimp x sweat for copper; crimp x PB for polybutylene repairs.
  • Ring and tool. Use copper crimp rings sized for the tubing and gauge every ring after crimping. Follow Viega instructions for approved tubing.

Common questions

Can PureFlow crimp fittings be used with a press tool?

No. PureFlow Crimp fittings use a separate copper crimp ring and a crimp tool. PureFlow Press fittings, which have a stainless steel sleeve attached, are the ones made for a press tool.

Which PureFlow crimp fitting connects PEX to copper?

The brass sweat adapters, listed as Crimp x Sweat or Crimp x FTG Sweat. One end is soldered to the copper and the other is crimped onto the PEX.

How do I check a crimp connection?

With the go/no-go gauge for that ring size: the go slot must pass over the crimped ring and the no-go slot must not. A ring that fails the gauge is cut off and replaced.

Related: Viega PureFlow press fittings, F1807 PEX crimp fittings, F2159 PEX fittings, PEX crimp tools and the full Viega range.

collection.descriptionHtml:
F1960 fittings are cold expansion fittings for PEX. The tubing and a PEX reinforcing ring are stretched with an expander tool, the fitting is inserted, and the tubing shrinks back onto the barb. There is no crimp ring to check with a gauge.

This collection covers ASTM F1960 fittings in 1/2" through 2", including reducing configurations, in composite and brass, plus lead-free brass adapters. Reducing tees are the largest group, with tees, manifolds, couplings, 90° elbows, drop ear elbows, plugs and expansion rings. Sweat, male, female, press and CPVC adapters cover transitions to copper and threaded systems. Brands are MrPEX Systems, HeatLink, Legend Valve, Sioux Chief and Webstone.

How to choose

  • Tubing. Expansion fittings rely on the tubing shrinking back, so use tubing its manufacturer lists for ASTM F1960 fittings. In practice that is PEX-A.
  • Size. 1/2", 3/4" and 1" for branch and distribution lines; 1-1/4", 1-1/2" and 2" for mains. Reducing tees list run x run x branch.
  • Body material. Composite or brass for tees, elbows and couplings; brass for threaded, sweat and press adapters.
  • Transition end. F1960 x sweat, x MNPT, x FNPT, x press or x CPVC, depending on what the PEX connects to.
  • Rings and tool. Each joint needs a PEX expansion ring of the same size and an expander tool with the matching head.

Common questions

What does ASTM F1960 cover?

ASTM F1960 is the standard specification for cold expansion fittings with PEX reinforcing rings for use with PEX and PE-RT tubing. A fitting marked F1960 is made to those dimensions.

Can F1960 fittings be crimped?

No. F1960 fittings are made for expanded tubing and a PEX reinforcing ring. Crimp connections use insert fittings made to ASTM F1807 or F2159 with a copper crimp ring.

Composite or brass expansion fittings?

Both are made to the same standard and install the same way. Composite covers most tees, elbows and couplings in this collection; brass is used where the fitting has a thread, a sweat end or a press end.

Related: PEX expansion tools, F1807 crimp fittings, F2159 PEX fittings, PEX manifolds, all PEX fittings.

collection.descriptionHtml:
F2159 fittings are plastic insert fittings for PEX tubing. The barbed fitting goes inside the tubing and is secured with a copper crimp ring or a stainless steel clamp. This collection covers ASTM F2159 fittings in 1/2" through 1", almost all in composite.

It includes MrPEX Systems, Sioux Chief and Legend Valve tees, reducing tees, 90° elbows, couplings, reducing couplings, male adapters and plugs, plus multi-port manifold tees. Legend Valve lists its fittings as PPSU plastic crimp/cinch fittings. The collection also holds a few press items, Viega PureFlow Press manifold tees and adapters and MrPEX press sleeves, which belong to separate press systems.

After crimping, check each joint with a go/no-go gauge, and verify that the tubing is listed for use with F2159 fittings.

How to choose

  • Tubing size. 1/2", 3/4" and 1". Reducing tees list run x run x branch in the title.
  • Standard. ASTM F2159 covers plastic insert fittings using a copper crimp ring, or alternate stainless steel clamps, for SDR9 PEX and PE-RT tubing. Metal insert fittings are covered by ASTM F1807.
  • Ring style. Copper crimp ring with a crimp tool, or stainless steel clamp with a cinch tool. Pick one system and use its gauge.
  • Configuration. Tee, reducing tee, elbow, coupling, plug or multi-port tee. For threaded and sweat transitions, see the brass adapters in the F1807 collection.

Common questions

What is the difference between F2159 and F1807 fittings?

Material. ASTM F2159 covers plastic insert fittings and ASTM F1807 covers metal insert fittings. Both are insert fittings secured on PEX tubing with a copper crimp ring.

Can I use stainless cinch clamps on F2159 fittings?

The current title of ASTM F2159 includes alternate stainless steel clamps, and Legend Valve lists its PPSU fittings as crimp/cinch. Confirm in the fitting manufacturer's instructions that clamps are approved for the fitting you buy.

Are F2159 fittings press fittings?

No. They are insert fittings closed with a crimp ring or clamp. The Viega PureFlow Press and MrPEX press sleeve items in this collection are the exception and need the matching press tool.

Related: F1807 crimp fittings, F1960 expansion fittings, Viega PureFlow press fittings, PEX crimp tools, all PEX fittings.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Gruvlok grooved fittings and couplings join pipe mechanically. A groove is rolled or cut near the pipe end, a gasket is seated over the joint and a housing is bolted around it, so the joint is made without welding or threading and can be taken apart for service.

This collection covers Gruvlok fittings in 2" through 12", with some 1" to 1-1/2" items, in painted, galvanized, 304 stainless and 316 stainless. It includes concentric and eccentric reducers, flange adapters, tees and reducing tees, threaded branch tees, end caps, 90°, 45° and 22-1/2° elbows, and SlideLok, RigidLok and Roughneck couplings, along with grooved butterfly valves, check valves and wye strainers. Most fittings are GR x GR or GR x GR x GR; adapters are GR x FPT, GR x MPT and GR x flange.

How to choose

  • Pipe size and material. Match the nominal size and choose painted or galvanized for carbon steel pipe, 304 or 316 stainless for stainless pipe. Grooved copper tube uses its own fittings.
  • Rigid or flexible coupling. Flexible couplings allow angular deflection and absorb thermal movement and vibration; rigid couplings do not. Use the type the system design calls for.
  • Gasket. Product titles show the gasket, for example EPDM (Green) or EPDM (Green & Red). Check the gasket grade against the fluid and temperature in the Gruvlok gasket chart; EPDM is the water-service grade and is not for petroleum service.
  • End configuration. GR is a grooved end. GR x FPT, GR x MPT and GR x flange fittings connect grooved pipe to threaded or flanged equipment.

Common questions

What is a SlideLok coupling?

SlideLok is Gruvlok's ready-for-installation rigid coupling (Figure 74). It slides onto the grooved pipe ends assembled, so the housing does not have to be taken apart before the bolts are tightened.

What does GR x GR mean?

Grooved by grooved: both ends of the fitting have a groove for a coupling. GR x GR x GR is a tee with three grooved ends, and a single GR is an end cap.

Which gasket comes on Gruvlok couplings here?

The couplings in this collection list EPDM gaskets, marked green or green and red. ASC Engineered Solutions gives a service temperature range for each gasket grade, so confirm the grade for your fluid and temperature before ordering.

Related: Gruvlok grooved copper fittings, all Gruvlok products, black iron threaded fittings, galvanized fittings for smaller threaded branch lines.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Black iron fittings are black malleable iron threaded fittings for gas, steam, compressed air and hydronic heating. This collection covers sizes 1/8" through 4" in FIP, MPT x FPT, three-way FPT and flanged configurations, almost all from Mueller Streamline.

Tees and reducing tees are the largest group, followed by couplings and reducing couplings, bushings, 90° elbows, street elbows, caps, unions, 45° elbows, plugs and floor flanges. Black iron is the usual choice on gas because it carries no zinc coating. Whether galvanized is also accepted for fuel gas depends on the local code and the gas utility.

Threads are NPT, a tapered thread: the joint tightens as the threads engage, so correct engagement depth matters. Thread engagement figures, Class 150 pressure ratings and Schedule 40 pipe dimensions are in our black iron reference guide.

How to choose

  • Size. Fittings are named by nominal pipe size, not measured diameter. 1/2", 3/4" and 1" are the common gas sizes; the range runs 1/8" to 4".
  • Connection ends. FIP (female) on tees, elbows, couplings and caps; MPT x FPT on street elbows and bushings; MIP on plugs; FPT x flange on floor flanges.
  • Reducing fittings. A reducing tee lists run x run x branch. A bushing reduces inside a fitting; a reducing coupling joins two pipe sizes.
  • Finish. Black for gas, steam, air and closed hydronic loops; galvanized where the outside of the fitting needs corrosion protection.
  • Thread sealant. Use a sealant rated for the medium. On fuel gas, use a PTFE tape or compound listed for gas.

Black iron fittings by size: Mueller Streamline part numbers

Common questions

Are black iron fittings used for gas?

Yes. Black malleable iron threaded fittings with steel pipe are a standard material for natural gas and propane piping inside buildings. Check the local fuel gas code and the gas utility for the materials they accept.

What is the difference between black iron and galvanized fittings?

The coating. Galvanized fittings are the same malleable iron castings with a zinc coating for corrosion resistance; black fittings have no zinc.

What is a street elbow?

An elbow with a male thread on one end and a female thread on the other (MPT x FPT). It threads directly into another fitting without a nipple.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Galvanized pipe fittings are malleable iron threaded fittings with a zinc coating. This collection covers Mueller Streamline galvanized fittings in 1/8" through 3", threaded NPT, in FIP, MPT x FPT, three-way FPT and flanged patterns.

Tees and reducing tees are the largest group, followed by couplings and reducing couplings, bushings, 90° elbows, street elbows, plugs, caps, floor flanges and 45° elbows. These are the same malleable iron castings used for black iron fittings; the zinc coating is the difference, and it is there for corrosion resistance on damp, exposed and outdoor runs.

Where galvanized steel meets copper in a water line, install a dielectric fitting between them, because the two metals in contact form a galvanic cell and the steel side corrodes at the joint.

How to choose

  • Size. Named by nominal pipe size, 1/8" to 3". 1/2", 3/4" and 1" are the most common.
  • Connection ends. FIP on tees, elbows and couplings; MPT x FPT on street elbows and bushings; MIP on plugs; FPT x flange on floor flanges.
  • Reducing fittings. Reducing tees list run x run x branch; reducing couplings and bushings list the large size first.
  • Service. Galvanized for water and for outdoor or damp locations. For fuel gas, check the local code and the gas utility before using galvanized; black iron is the usual material.

Common questions

Can galvanized fittings be used on gas lines?

It depends on the local code and the gas utility. Black iron is the usual material for fuel gas, so confirm before installing galvanized.

Can I connect galvanized pipe directly to copper?

Not directly in a water line. Use a dielectric union or dielectric nipple between the two metals to separate them.

Do galvanized and black iron fittings have the same threads?

Yes. Both are NPT tapered pipe threads in the same nominal sizes, so a 3/4" galvanized fitting and a 3/4" black fitting thread onto the same pipe.

Related: galvanized nipples, black iron fittings, dielectric fittings, thread sealant and PTFE tape. For 2" and larger steel pipe, Gruvlok grooved fittings and couplings join pipe without threading or welding.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Brass pipe fittings are threaded fittings for potable water, air and general service. This collection covers Legend Valve no-lead cast bronze threaded fittings in 1/8" through 3", in FIP, FIP x MIP and MIP patterns, plus a few MIP x AWWA meter couplings for water service work.

Hex bushings and reducing couplings are the largest groups, followed by couplings, caps, plugs, tees and reducing tees, 90° and 45° elbows, street elbows and unions. Legend Valve identifies these fittings as no lead (part numbers ending in NL), and its submittal cites ASME B16.15 for cast bronze threaded fittings and ASME B1.20.1 for the pipe threads.

Anything installed on a potable water line must be lead free, so check the marking on the fitting.

How to choose

  • Size. Nominal pipe size from 1/8" to 3". Bushings and reducing couplings list the large size first.
  • Thread ends. FNPT x FNPT for couplings, elbows and tees; MNPT x FNPT for bushings and street elbows; MNPT for plugs; MIP x AWWA for meter couplings.
  • Lead content. For potable water choose no-lead fittings. Legend Valve certifies its lead-free bronze fittings to NSF/ANSI 372.
  • Fitting type. A bushing reduces inside a fitting, a reducing coupling joins two pipe sizes, and a union lets the line be taken apart without cutting.

Common questions

Are these brass fittings lead free?

The Legend Valve fittings in this collection are listed as no-lead cast bronze, with part numbers ending in NL. Legend Valve states they are third-party certified to NSF/ANSI 372.

What is the difference between brass and bronze fittings?

Both are copper alloys and both are sold as "brass fittings". The Legend Valve threaded fittings here are listed as no-lead cast bronze.

What does FIP x MIP mean?

Female iron pipe thread by male iron pipe thread, the same as FNPT x MNPT. It describes a fitting with a female thread on one end and a male thread on the other, such as a bushing or street elbow.

Related: brass nipples, compression fittings, water service fittings, dielectric fittings and the full Legend Valve range.

collection.descriptionHtml:
ABS pipe fittings in this collection are DWV fittings for drain, waste and vent systems. Sizes run 1-1/2" through 6", in all-hub, hub x hub, hub x spigot and threaded configurations, mostly from Charlotte Pipe with Sioux Chief, Nibco, Canplas and HoldRite.

Wyes, sanitary tees, tee-wye combinations, double wyes, double sanitary tees and double fixture tees make up most of the range, along with 90°, 45° and 22-1/2° elbows, street elbows, couplings, flush bushings, female adapters, caps, cleanout plugs, test tees and closet flanges.

ABS is joined with solvent cement made for ABS, which is not interchangeable with PVC cement. A sanitary tee is used where flow turns from horizontal to vertical; where it turns from vertical to horizontal, codes call for a wye or combination.

How to choose

  • Pipe size. 1-1/2" and 2" for fixture drains and vents, 3" and 4" for stacks and building drains, 6" for larger mains. Reducing fittings list every size.
  • Ends. H (hub) accepts pipe; spigot is pipe-sized and goes into a hub, which is how street fittings and flush bushings work; FPT and MPT ends take threaded plugs and adapters.
  • Fitting pattern. Sanitary tee, wye, combination tee-wye, or long-turn elbow, chosen by the direction of flow your plumbing code allows.
  • Material match. Use ABS DWV fittings with ABS DWV pipe. DWV fittings are for non-pressure drainage and are not for pressure piping.
  • Closet flanges. Choose by pipe size (3", 4" or 4" x 3"), hub or spigot fit, and ring type.

Common questions

Do ABS fittings need primer?

ABS DWV joints are made with ABS solvent cement. Whether a primer is used depends on the cement manufacturer's instructions and your local code.

Can ABS fittings be glued to PVC pipe?

ABS cement and PVC cement are not interchangeable. Where ABS meets PVC, use the transition method your plumbing code accepts, such as a listed transition cement or a mechanical coupling.

What does "All H" or "H x Spigot" mean in a fitting name?

H is a hub, the socket that pipe glues into. "All H" means every opening is a hub. "H x Spigot" means one end is a hub and the other is a spigot the size of pipe, which fits into the hub of another fitting.

Related: PVC DWV fittings, no-hub cast iron fittings, solvent cements, cleanouts, shielded transition couplings.

collection.descriptionHtml:
PVC DWV fittings are solvent-weld fittings for drain, waste and vent systems. This collection covers sizes 1-1/2" through 10", in all-hub, hub x hub, hub x spigot and threaded configurations, mostly from Charlotte Pipe, with HoldRite TestRite test tees and Sioux Chief closet flanges.

Wyes, sanitary tees and tee-wye combinations lead the range, with 45°, 22-1/2° and 90° elbows, long-turn and street elbows, couplings, reducing couplings, flush bushings, cleanout adapters and plugs, caps, P-traps and closet flanges. A few PVC no-hub test tees connect to cast iron systems.

DWV fittings are not pressure rated. Charlotte Pipe makes its molded PVC DWV fittings to ASTM D 2665 and states they are not intended for pressure use, so do not put one on a supply line even though it resembles a Schedule 40 pressure fitting.

How to choose

  • Pipe size. 1-1/2" and 2" for fixture drains and vents, 3" and 4" for stacks and building drains, 6" to 10" for larger mains.
  • Ends. H (hub) accepts pipe; spigot fits into a hub; FPT and MPT ends take cleanout plugs and threaded adapters.
  • Fitting pattern. Wye, combination, sanitary tee or long-turn elbow, chosen by the direction of flow your plumbing code allows. A sanitary tee is for horizontal-to-vertical flow.
  • Joining. Charlotte Pipe specifies a two-step solvent weld: primer conforming to ASTM F 656, then solvent cement conforming to ASTM D 2564.
  • DWV or pressure. For pressure piping use Schedule 40 or Schedule 80 pressure fittings instead. Our PVC & CPVC pipe dimensions and specifications explain the difference.

Common questions

Can PVC DWV fittings be used for pressure?

No. Charlotte Pipe states its PVC DWV fittings are not intended for pressure use. They are made for gravity drain, waste and vent systems.

Do PVC DWV fittings need primer?

Charlotte Pipe specifies a two-step process for PVC solvent-weld joints: a primer conforming to ASTM F 656 followed by a solvent cement conforming to ASTM D 2564. Follow your local code.

What is a TestRite test tee?

A HoldRite DWV test and cleanout tee with a plug. This collection has PVC and PVC no-hub versions.

Related: ABS DWV fittings, PVC Schedule 40 pressure fittings, solvent cements, primers, cleanouts.

No-hub cast iron pipe fittings are hubless soil fittings for drain, waste and vent systems. Pipe and fittings butt together and are joined with a shielded coupling, a neoprene gasket inside a stainless steel shield, tightened to the specified torque. No lead and oakum are used.

This collection covers Tyler Pipe no-hub fittings in 1-1/2" through 12", with 2", 3", 4" and 6" the most common sizes. It includes sanitary tees and wyes with reducing and double patterns, combinations, crosses, concentric reducers, 1/4, 1/8 and 1/16 bends, short and long sweep elbows, P-traps, cleanout tees, plugs and closet flanges. Connection patterns are NH x NH, three-way and four-way, plus NH x FPT and NH x flange. Tyler Pipe makes its no-hub pipe and fittings to CISPI 301 and ASTM A 888.

How to choose

  • Size. Nominal size from 1-1/2" to 12". Reducing tees, wyes and combos list run x run x branch.
  • Pattern. Sanitary tee, wye, combination or bend, chosen by the direction of flow your plumbing code allows. Bends are named by fraction: 1/4 bend is 90°, 1/8 bend is 45°, 1/16 bend is 22-1/2°.
  • Ends. NH is a plain no-hub end for a coupling. NH x FPT fittings are tapped for a threaded connection or cleanout plug.
  • Couplings. Couplings are sold separately. Check which coupling type your code or specification requires.
  • Standard. CISPI 301 / ASTM A 888 for hubless cast iron soil pipe and fittings.

Common questions

How are no-hub cast iron fittings joined?

With a no-hub coupling: a neoprene sleeve over the two plain ends, covered by a stainless steel shield with clamps tightened to the coupling manufacturer's torque.

What standard covers no-hub cast iron fittings?

CISPI 301 and ASTM A 888 cover hubless cast iron soil pipe and fittings for sanitary, storm drain, waste and vent piping. Tyler Pipe lists both for its no-hub line.

Can no-hub cast iron connect to plastic pipe?

Yes, with a transition coupling sized for both materials. Outside diameters differ between cast iron and plastic, so choose a coupling listed for that exact pair.

Related: shielded couplings, unshielded couplings, ABS DWV fittings, PVC DWV fittings and the full Tyler Pipe range.

Viega products here cover press-connection piping and radiant heating. The largest groups are Viega ProPress fittings for copper tube in 1/2" through 4", MegaPress and MegaPressG fittings for steel pipe, and PureFlow Press and PureFlow Crimp fittings for PEX.

The range also includes MegaPress 316 stainless fittings, press ball valves with ProPress and MegaPressG ends, red-stripe oxygen barrier PEX tubing, stainless steel manifolds with actuators, and heat transfer plates and panels for radiant floors. Product titles give the Viega model number, the sizes and the connection in parentheses, such as P-P for press by press or P-FPT for press by female thread.

Choose the fitting family that matches the pipe material and the fluid, then the size and end connections, and confirm that your press tool and jaws are compatible with that fitting line.

How to choose

  • ProPress for copper. For Type K, L and M hard copper tube in 1/2" to 4" and soft copper in 1/2" to 1-1/4", with EPDM sealing elements.
  • MegaPress for steel pipe. Zinc-nickel coated carbon steel fittings for Schedule 5 to Schedule 40 steel pipe. MegaPressG, with an HNBR sealing element, is the version for fuel gas.
  • PureFlow for PEX. PureFlow Press fittings have a stainless sleeve attached and need a press tool; PureFlow Crimp fittings use a copper crimp ring.
  • End connections. P is press, FTG is a tube-sized or pipe-sized street end, FPT and MPT are threads. The code is in every title.
  • Tool. Confirm that your press tool and jaws are approved for the fitting family and size.

Common questions

What is the difference between ProPress and MegaPress?

The pipe they join. ProPress fittings are copper and bronze fittings for copper tube. MegaPress fittings are carbon steel fittings for IPS steel pipe, with MegaPressG for fuel gas and MegaPress 316 for stainless steel pipe.

What is Viega Smart Connect?

A feature of Viega press fittings that lets an unpressed fitting be identified during pressure testing. Viega states it does not replace the pressure test required by code.

Do ProPress fittings work on PEX?

No. ProPress is for copper tube. For PEX, Viega makes PureFlow Press and PureFlow Crimp fittings, and transition fittings with a PureFlow Press end and a ProPress end connect the two systems.

Viega collections: copper press fittings (ProPress), Viega MegaPress fittings, gas press fittings (MegaPressG), PureFlow press fittings, PureFlow crimp fittings.

Gruvlok products here are grooved couplings and grooved-end fittings for mechanical piping. A grooved coupling is a bolted housing with a gasket that closes over the grooved ends of two pipes or fittings to make the joint.

The range has two systems. Gruvlok steel fittings, in painted, galvanized and stainless, cover 45° and 90° elbows, tees, reducing tees, concentric and eccentric reducers, end caps, flange adapters and couplings in sizes up to 12", along with grooved butterfly valves, check valves and wye strainers. Gruvlok copper fittings cover tees, couplings, elbows, reducers and caps for grooved copper tube in 2" to 6". Coupling types include SlideLok, RigidLok and Roughneck, reducing couplings and outlet couplings.

How to choose

  • Pipe material. Grooved systems are specific to pipe material: use copper-system fittings and couplings on grooved copper tube and steel-system parts on steel pipe.
  • Size. Match the nominal pipe size; reducing fittings and reducing couplings list both sizes.
  • Coupling type. Rigid couplings such as SlideLok hold the joint fixed; flexible couplings allow deflection and movement. Use the type the design calls for.
  • Gasket. Confirm the gasket grade for the service temperature and fluid. Titles show the gasket where one is included, for example EPDM (Green & Red).
  • Finish. Painted or galvanized for carbon steel pipe; 304 or 316 stainless for stainless pipe.

Common questions

What is a grooved coupling?

A two-piece or hinged housing that bolts around a gasket and engages a groove near the end of each pipe. The housing holds the pipes together and the gasket seals the joint, so no welding or threading is needed.

What is the difference between a rigid and a flexible grooved coupling?

A rigid coupling clamps the grooved ends so the joint does not move. A flexible coupling allows limited angular deflection and expansion or contraction at the joint.

Do Gruvlok steel couplings fit grooved copper tube?

No. Copper tube has different outside diameters and groove dimensions than steel pipe, so grooved copper uses the Gruvlok copper-system couplings and fittings.

Gruvlok collections: Gruvlok fittings and couplings for steel pipe and Gruvlok grooved copper fittings. Related: copper press fittings and black iron threaded fittings.

Mueller Streamline products in our catalog center on pipe fittings for water, gas and hydronic work. The range includes wrought copper sweat fittings in C x C and C x C x C configurations, black iron elbows, tees, couplings, caps, plugs, bushings and unions from 1/8" up, copper press fittings for copper tube in 1/2" to 4", black iron nipples, and galvanized fittings and nipples.

The catalog also includes carbon steel press fittings for gas and for mechanical piping, cleaned and bagged copper fittings, copper DWV fittings, and pre-insulated copper line sets for HVAC refrigerant piping.

Match the fitting material to the pipe: threaded black iron for gas and steel lines, copper sweat or press fittings for copper tube.

How to choose

  • Pipe material. Copper sweat or copper press fittings for copper tube; black or galvanized malleable iron for threaded steel pipe; carbon steel press fittings for plain-end steel pipe.
  • Joining method. Sweat fittings are soldered. Press fittings need a press tool and jaws that Mueller approves for the Streamline press line. Threaded fittings need thread sealant.
  • End connection. C is a solder cup, FTG a fitting end, P a press end, FIP and MIP are pipe threads. Confirm whether a reducing or street pattern is needed.
  • Size. Copper fittings are named by nominal tube size and iron fittings by nominal pipe size; a 3/4" copper fitting does not fit 3/4" steel pipe.
  • Service. For gas press work, choose the gas-rated carbon steel press fittings (part numbers ending in G), not the mechanical ones.

Common questions

What tube do Mueller Streamline copper press fittings fit?

Mueller lists its Streamline copper press fittings for ASTM B88 Type K, L and M tube: hard-drawn copper in 1/2" to 4" and soft copper in 1/2" to 1-1/4". The fittings use an EPDM O-ring.

What is the difference between C x C and FTG x C copper fittings?

C is a cup that accepts tube. FTG is a fitting end with the outside diameter of tube, which goes into the cup of another fitting. FTG x C fittings, such as street elbows, connect fitting to fitting without a piece of tube.

Are Streamline press fittings and sweat fittings interchangeable?

They fit the same copper tube sizes but are joined differently: sweat fittings are soldered, press fittings are pressed onto the tube and seal on an O-ring. Use one method per joint.

Mueller Streamline collections: copper sweat fittings, copper press fittings, black iron fittings, galvanized iron fittings.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Sioux Chief products in the catalog span drainage and rough-in plumbing. Items include cleanouts, adjustable floor drains, shower drains, ABS and PVC closet flanges and urinal flange kits, backwater valves, and PVC, ABS and chrome P-traps with trap adapters, center and end outlet wastes, disposer kits and branch tailpieces.

On the supply side the range covers F1807 crimp, F1960 expansion and F2159 composite PEX fittings, PEX service boxes, water hammer arresters, escutcheons and tube hangers.

For tubular drain parts, match the tube diameter (1-1/4" or 1-1/2"), material and joint type, slip joint or solvent weld. For drains, cleanouts and closet flanges, confirm the pipe size and material the body connects to. For PEX fittings, match the connection standard your tool uses.

How to choose

  • Pipe material. Drains, cleanouts and closet flanges are made for a specific pipe: PVC, ABS or cast iron. The material is in the product title.
  • Pipe size and fit. Closet flanges and cleanouts come in hub (over the pipe) and spigot or inside-fit (into the pipe or hub) versions.
  • PEX connection standard. F1807 and F2159 are crimp insert fittings; F1960 fittings need expansion tubing and an expander tool. Part numbers and titles state the standard.
  • Tubular size. 1-1/4" or 1-1/2"; check the trap and tailpiece before ordering.

Popular in this collection: Sioux Chief 687-2XD PEX Single Valve Service Box, Sioux Chief 598-023 Expansion Tank Bracket, Sioux Chief 869-2A 2" ABS Backwater Valve.

Common questions

What does a backwater valve do?

A backwater valve lets wastewater flow out of the building but closes if the sewer backs up, so sewage cannot come back in through floor drains and low fixtures. Match the valve to the pipe size and material, such as 2" ABS.

Why support an expansion tank with a bracket?

A thermal expansion tank full of water is heavy, and hanging it from the water heater piping puts that weight on the fittings. A bracket such as the Sioux Chief 598-023 carries the tank so the piping does not have to.

F1807 crimp or F1960 expansion PEX fittings?

They are different systems with different tools. F1807 fittings are crimped with a copper or stainless ring; F1960 fittings need expansion PEX tubing and an expansion tool. Match the fitting to the system already installed. See F1807 crimp fittings.

Related: cleanouts, floor drains, P-traps, F1807 crimp fittings, ABS DWV fittings.
